title: Montreal residents protest Bill C-39 outside Industry Minister's office

tea.why: Protesters oppose Bill C-39, arguing it threatens environmental protections, Indigenous rights, and workers' rights.
tea.want: Opponents demand the government stop the bill, which they claim prioritizes corporate interests over environmental and Indigenous concerns.
tea.changed: Nov 12: Residents held three separate demonstrations across Montreal, including one at the office of Industry Minister Mélanie Joly.

summary: On November 12, 2026, residents in Montreal held three separate protests against the federal government's Bill C-39, also known as the Building Canada Strong Act. One demonstration took place outside the constituency office of Industry Minister Mélanie Joly. The actions were part of a nationwide day of mobilization coordinated by the Canadian chapter of 350.org. Organizers included Common Horizon, Équiterre, Mères au front, Greenpeace, and Seniors for Climate Action Now. Participants expressed concerns that the bill would expedite project reviews at the expense of environmental safeguards and Indigenous treaty rights. Speakers criticized the government's focus on corporate interests and called for investments in sustainable industries. Minister Joly was not present at her office during the protest. No official response from the government regarding the specific demonstrations was reported in the provided sources.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Protesters gathered outside the office of Industry Minister Mélanie Joly and two other locations in Montreal as part of a nationwide day of action.

sources.title: Environment activists protest outside Mélanie Joly
